body_markdown:
When you’re a driving enthusiast, you never stop thinking about where (and what) you’d like to drive. For those of us in the Midwest, the end of driving season never fails to prompt a flurry of fresh ideas, just as the window for salt-free driving comes to a close. Even if your local weather doesn’t force your special car (or cars) into seasonal storage in the winter, fall is an ideal time to reflect on the wins of this past summer and spend a little time planning ahead for the next one. And if your special car wasn’t in driving shape this summer, there’s no better motivation to make progress than planning the adventures you’ll take in the finished project.


Here are the trips that are on our minds for 2027. We hope that they help you spool up your own road-trip ideas for next year—share them with us in the comments below!


## Lake Erie Coastal Ohio Scenic Byway


Flickr/Mike Mekinda


At the beginning of this year’s driving season, I mentioned bombing through the Appalachians. I did not get to do that, but I’m still happy with the ground that I covered. Next year, though, I want to take the Centurion on the[Lake Erie Coastal Ohio Scenic Byway](https://www.transportation.ohio.gov/travel/driving/byways/lake-erie-coastal-ohio-trail-byway) . The route courses through Ohio farmland, cities, and small towns, with, as you may have guessed, Lake Erie alongside for most of it. Cruising top-down at 45 mph[on a couch with wheels](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/beloved-buick-the-centurion-rides-again/) seems like a good way to unwind. Plus, the route goes past one of the best amusement parks in the country, Cedar Point. *— Eddy Eckart*


## Florida’s Gulf Coast


Unsplash/Anita Denunzio


Next season? You mean we aren’t allowed to drive in all four seasons? As a resident of the Gulf Coast, I take issue with the scope of this question!


In all seriousness, I am kinda hooked on Lemons Rallies, after celebrating my Lincoln Mark VIII’s 30th Birthday[on one last year](https://www.hagerty.com/media/great-reads/i-celebrated-my-30th-birthday-on-a-lemons-rally/) . So this winter, I am taking Interstate 10 down Florida-way to participate in the[final Lemons Rally of 2026](https://24hoursoflemons.com/rally-details/?id=427) . I am quite looking forward to seeing places like Panama City and to getting out of the house and watching the odometer rack up some miles. I likely won’t experience any fun driving roads, but maybe I can convince our own Steven Cole Smith to join me on the rally. As a local, he can add some spice to the journey. The only remaining variable is a doozy, because I still don’t know what car I am driving! *— Sajeev Mehta*


## The Scottish Highlands


Unsplash/Colin Horn


Unsplash/K B


The Highlands are calling. I’ve explored much of Scotland, but never completed the full North Coast 500 route. It’s a big loop that starts and finishes in Inverness, following the coastline via John O’Groats (the northernmost point in mainland UK). Along the way, there are stunning sandy beaches, breathtaking bridge crossings, and the awesome Applecross Pass to conquer. Without giving too much away, the plan is to make the challenge even greater with a group of pals and some cars that may well find the 500-mile route just a bit too much. Stay tuned. *— Nik Berg*


## Kansas Plains


Kyle Smith


My annual trip from Traverse City, Michigan, to McPherson, Kansas, will be happening the first week of May as usual, but don’t you think for a second that the routine nature of the trip means I’m not excited about it. With any luck, the car of choice next year will be something at least a few decades old, and the trip will become more than the usual one-day solitary confinement inside a modern car. It’s not the most scenic drive, but it has come to be a trip that provides room for thinking and processing, which I don’t often do without being forced to sit still like that. A good thing, and one I’m very much looking forward to. *— Kyle Smith*


## Banff National Park


UCG/Universal Images Group/Getty Images


DeAgostini/Getty Images


Alan Dyer/VW Pics/Getty Images


With my second child due in early 2027, I must report that I have no exciting drives planned for next year, except the one to the hospital. But amid the late nights and groggy mornings, I will be doing a whole lot of *daydreaming* about my next big adventure. I’d love to go to Banff National Park in Alberta, Canada. From what I’ve read, the roads are gorgeous but not optimal for spirited driving, given the park speed limits and such. But a great road is not always about that, as much as it’s about the world it opens up. The scenery here is immaculate in photos, but in person I suspect it’s breathtaking. Hiking, rock climbing, wildlife photography, camping, stargazing—bring it all on! *— Eric Weiner*


## Staying Local


Jeffrey Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images


If we’re talking season as in the spring/summer/fall/winter sense, I’m chomping at the bit to get to fall. Our first child is due any day now, so part of me wanted to respond to this question with “the drive from my house to the hospital,” or the inverse of that, but I’ll dream bigger.


I’d love to get the whole family—wife, newborn, big doof of a Golden Retriever—into my truck for a lovely day trip. Maybe we’ll scamper north to Charlevoix, or perhaps we’ll head northeast and visit the Boyne area, maybe take the chairlift to the top of the ski hill during peak fall colors. Who knows. Life is about to change in a massive way for me, and I’m so excited. I have a feeling any drive not conducted in a hurried way is going to feel that extra bit special because of the new cargo. *— Nate Petroelje*


## East Coast Cruise


Unsplash/Raphael Assouline


My wife and I have been thinking of a New England road trip for a while, so that’s the one that we’ve been daydreaming about lately. We’ve visited lots of National Parks in the West, including several in Washington, California, Hawaii, Arizona, Colorado, Nevada, Wyoming, and a bunch in Utah, but we’ve never been to the East Coast together. Acadia National Park is probably the next on the to-do list. *— Brandan Gillogly*


## Up North in Michigan


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


The temperatures in Detroit dipped below 50 for the first time this morning, and while I am in a mood to park myself at the nearest brewery in celebration (or drive seven hours north to Marquette to sit at my favorite brewery there), this question is about next year.


This summer was a busy one. Next year, I’m hoping to slow down and soak in some sun by a lakeshore. Michigan has a lot of that, and while I love a good east-coast-Michigan experience in Saugatuck, the most peaceful summer moments I’ve enjoyed have been “up north,” with a book and a sandwich, in some quiet nook of a beach. That’s the prize at the end of the road trip for me, so even if my road-tripping chariot is no more spine-tingling than[Precious the Prius](https://www.hagerty.com/media/advice/piston-slap/piston-slap-premonitions-for-the-precious-prius/) , the trip will be well worth it. I’ll skip I-75 as much as possible, and trace the two-lane state highways northwest of Lansing instead. *— Grace Jarvis*
